name: Central Bank of India
title: Central Bank of India - 532885 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Central Bank of India Q2 FY27 net profit rose 21% YoY to Rs1,469 Crore, with NIM at 3.01% and gross NPA at 2.39%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs1,469 Crore (up 21% YoY, 11% QoQ), with operating profit of Rs2,268 Crore and NII of Rs4,146 Crore (up 26.28% YoY). Global advances grew 29.83% to Rs3,81,032 Crore and domestic deposits grew 14.41%, with CASA at 44.65%, below the 48% plus or minus 1% guidance. Asset quality improved on net NPA (0.31%) and slippage (0.24%), but credit cost rose to 0.53% as provisions were built for standard assets and ahead of ECL. Cost-to-income at 58.95% missed the sub-56% guidance.

guidance was above 3%; down about 5bps QoQ per analyst

financial_highlights.metric: Yield on advances / cost of deposits

segments.name: RAM (retail, agri, MSME)
segments.commentary: RAM book Rs2,54,273 Crore, up 21%; retail Rs1,12,299 Crore (+24.49%), agriculture Rs67,778 Crore (+19.92%), MSME Rs74,196 Crore (+17.36%). RAM:corporate mix 68:32 against 65:35 plus or minus 5% guidance.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate book Rs1,18,666 Crore, up about 42-44% YoY from Rs83,000 Crore; focus on roads, infrastructure, data centres, renewables. Pipeline: Rs7,000 Crore undisbursed sanctions, Rs5,200 Crore under process, Rs11,000 Crore under consideration.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book Rs41,000 Crore at average yield above 8.5%; plan to open or customise 116 gold loan branches with TAT up to 30 minutes.

segments.name: Overseas / GIFT City
segments.commentary: GIFT City branch opened June 29, 2026, contributing overseas advances of Rs8,093 Crore. FCNR(B) raised USD 926.74 million across 731 accounts; overseas loans against it USD 794.60 million.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Yield rose to 7.19% at September 30, 2026 and was reported higher at 7.25-7.40% since; AFS book Rs1,023 Crore (from Rs843 Crore). Treasury earned Rs56 Crore from IPO participation; management sees treasury outlook as challenged.

guidance_outlook: Management says ECL requires Rs5,000-5,500 Crore in total, with Rs1,525 Crore already provided; ECL applies from April 1, 2027. Whether to take a one-time hit or stagger it is undecided.
Credit cost guided at up to 0.75% for next year as well (0.53% this quarter).
ROA expected to stay above 1%, supported by rising repo rates on 61% external-benchmark-linked book; management declined to guide beyond next year.
NIM expected to rise in a rising-rate scenario; management says margin increase is likely.
Recoveries from written-off pool (Rs31,301 Crore) targeted at Rs2,500 Crore-plus this year; aviation account expected to yield Rs700 Crore via SARFAESI in the current or next quarter.
Cost-to-income: management says efficiency numbers will improve in coming quarters, but Q2 missed the sub-56% guidance.
Business growth guidance of 14-15%, deposit growth 10-12% and advances growth 14-16% were all exceeded in Q2.
capex_capacity: 116 gold loan branches to be opened or customised with TAT up to 30 minutes.
300 marketing officers recruited; 32 places identified for MSME credit teams; CPAC revamped for higher ticket loans.
Credit card franchise to launch around June; cash management services with two modules live and more in coming months.
New banking emerging department (NBET) set up to lead digital user experience; 45 digital journeys launched and under revision.
demand_pricing: Management said yield on advances was 7.87% and cost of deposits 4.60%; the 125bp reference rate cut in the prior year hit the book.
Gold loans, SHG linkages (26 states NRLM tie-ups) and housing (over 50% of retail advances) named as growth engines; car loans via dealer and builder tie-ups.
Average ticket size is rising for housing and car loans, per management; a Rs22 Crore green home loan was cited.
Corporate growth focus on renewable energy, roads, data centres, real estate, hospitality, NBFC and agri-food processing.

qa_highlights.question: How much ECL provisioning is needed and is the bank prepared?
qa_highlights.answer: Total requirement Rs5,000-5,500 Crore, with Rs1,525 Crore already provided; management is confident profits can cover the gap before April 1, 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Will the one-time ECL hit go to net worth on April 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the difference over Rs1,525 Crore is the remaining need; it has not decided between a one-time hit and staggering it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did provisions rise even as NPA and slippage improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited building a higher provision coverage ratio in good times and standard-asset provisions rising to Rs399 Crore from Rs37 Crore (prior year); credit cost 0.53%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ROA of about 1% sustainable into FY28 and FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROA should stay above 1% but declined to guide beyond next year given fast-changing conditions, citing El Nino and global factors.

qa_highlights.question: Why is yield on advances low versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the 125bp reference rate cut on the 61% external-benchmark book; repo pass-through lags and yields should rise as rates increase; gold loans yield above 8.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Any stress in rural collections from El Nino or drought?
qa_highlights.answer: Management saw no distress signals this quarter, except some agri slippage in Pune; it will assess the drought impact with future data.

risks_watch: CASA ratio at 44.65% versus 48% plus or minus 1% guidance, with FCNR(B) mobilisation cited as a reason.
Cost-to-income at 58.95% against guidance of below 56%.
ECL transition of Rs5,000-5,500 Crore from April 1, 2027; treatment (one-time or staggered) not yet decided.
Treasury headwinds from rising yields (7.19% at September 30, 2026, later 7.25-7.40%) and mark-to-market pressure on AFS.
El Nino and possible drought effects on rural and agri asset quality.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and recoveries; candid about misses on CASA and cost-to-income. Cautious and non-committal on FY28 ROA, ECL treatment and treasury outlook.
key_quotes: I am fully confident that ROA is going to be above 1%.
Our growth is still more than 9%. The low-cost deposits mobilization is not a challenge for us.
Here, due to obvious reason, due to FCNR(B) mobilization and other aspects, we could not meet the market guidance, and we closed at 44.65%

adds.what: 116 gold loan branches to be opened or customised (TAT up to 30 minutes)

growth.why: Management guides business growth of 14-15% (advances 14-16%, deposits 10-12%), all exceeded in Q2; backing is a Rs7,000 Cr undisbursed corporate sanction pipeline plus Rs5,200 Cr under process and gold/retail/SHG growth engines, but no new capacity with numbers beyond 116 gold branches and GIFT City, and CASA missed its 48% guide.
